study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Ma et al., Journal of Behavioral Addictions, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Comparative analysis of cortical anatomy in male participants with internet gaming disorder or tobacco use disorder: Insights from normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly state the study aims and the purpose of applying normative modeling: to analyze cortical thickness (CT) development patterns in IGD and TUD, assess similarities/differences, and support understanding of whether IGD qualifies as an addiction. The rationale for normative modeling as an individual-level framework is described, including mapping deviations from typical development.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "This study utilized normative modeling to analyze the cortical thickness (CT) development patterns of male patients with IGD and TUD, aiming to provide further insights into whether IGD qualifies as an addiction."; "To this end, this study aims to expand our knowledge regarding the neural mechanism of IGD and TUD by investigating CT development patterns."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: A new normative model is built using healthy controls from the GSP dataset. The study cites the original GSP publication and link, reports image quality standards (CAT12 IQR threshold; Euler index site-adjusted threshold) and exclusion procedures, and provides final sample sizes with reasons for exclusion (age/education matching removed 2 TUD; QC excluded 8 IGD, 1 TUD by IQR; 2 IGD, 6 TUD by Euler; none in HC).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Data of 665 male participants were downloaded from the Brain Genomics Superstruct Project (GSP)... Age and education level matching... resulting in the exclusion of 2 participants from the TUD group. The quality control process ... yielded a final sample of 68... 71... and 665..."; "All participants with IQR ratings below 'C-' were excluded (no participants were excluded in HC, while 8 were excluded in the IGD and 1 in the TUD)... excluded participants with square roots greater than 10... (no participants were excluded in HC, while 2 were excluded in the IGD and 6 in the TUD)."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and Euler index are included as covariates in the normative model. The dataset is multi-site (GSP) and site/scanner effects are partially addressed via Euler-based QC and additional checks, but site is not modeled explicitly as a covariate nor via harmonization methods (e.g., ComBat, hierarchical modeling).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "... predict the entire brain based on participants' age and euler index as covariates."; "The effects of scanner artifacts were mitigated by performing additional checks (Fig. 1F)."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort is from the GSP dataset; the study names the dataset, cites the original publication, and provides the data access link.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "... downloaded from the Brain Genomics Superstruct Project (GSP), a large-scale, multi-site brain imaging study (Holmes et al., 2015). Each site participating in the GSP had obtained informed consent... (link provided)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guide: For SECONDARY data (existing datasets) used as the reference cohort, answer NA. The reference cohort (HC) comes from the GSP dataset.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing uses CAT12 within SPM12 for SBM; cortical parcellation with Desikan–Killiany; QC procedures are described using CAT12 IQR ratings and Euler index with explicit exclusion thresholds and counts.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Raw MRI images were processed and analyzed using ... CAT-12 ... integrated in ... SPM-12 ..."; "Cortical parcellation was conducted using the Desikan-Killiany atlas... All participants with IQR ratings below 'C-' were excluded ... Euler index ... excluded participants ..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative range in the HC cohort was estimated using 10-fold cross-validation, ensuring that model performance is evaluated on data not used for fitting in each fold.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The normative range of the model in the HC group was estimated through 10-fold cross-validation and then applied to patients."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset is reported for evaluating the normative model. The model is trained/validated via 10-fold CV on HC and then applied to patient cohorts; no external HC validation is described.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "... estimated through 10-fold cross-validation and then applied to patients."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The study specifies Gaussian Process Regression implemented via PCNtoolkit with age and Euler index covariates, uses empirical Bayes and ROI-level t-tests, and details cross-validation and thresholds. However, key model settings such as kernel choice and hyperparameters are not reported.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "The Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit (PCNtoolkit) ... The model estimated using Gaussian process regression (GPR) ... The normative range ... 10-fold cross-validation ... parameters were estimated using training data with empirical Bayesian estimation ..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: The paper does not report quantitative model fit metrics (e.g., R^2, correlation, prediction error, calibration/coverage) for the HC reference cohort. It qualitatively notes that HC generally did not show significant deviations at Z=1.65, but no explicit numeric performance metrics are provided.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "At a threshold Z value of 1.65 (p = 0.05), the HC group in general did not show significant deviations from the normative model, indicating the good fit of this model for this cohort."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is used, the study does not report sample sizes or demographic characteristics for each fold/partition of the reference cohort.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "... estimated through 10-fold cross-validation ..." (no additional details on partition characteristics).
